name: Aphex Twin
hook: Home-made techno from Cornwall, begun as a teenager, that Warp packaged for listening rather than dancing.
blurb: Richard D. James grew up in Cornwall and started recording on cassette around 1985, when he was about 13. His first album, Selected Ambient Works 85–92, came out in 1992 on a Belgian label and collected those early tracks; its title is where the 1985 start year here comes from. That same year Warp put one of his tracks, as The Dice Man, first on its Artificial Intelligence compilation, which presented this music as something for home listening and shaped how it was heard. He then signed to Warp, first as Polygon Window and then as Aphex Twin. His early work is often described as made on modified or home-built equipment, but James has told contradictory stories about his gear and his past, so claims about it are held loosely here.
